report.source_text: The patient deferred treatment options during her hospital stay and was discharged in stable condition after receiving diuretics with the improvement of her lower extremity edema, shortness of breath, and orthopnea. Upon follow-up with the patient’s primary care provider, the patient endorsed continued improvement of her functional status while on maintenance diuretics. The patient decided against bulk resection of her tumor with the surgical team; however, she started targeted molecular therapy with imatinib 100 mg twice daily.

clinician.trajectory_summary: An 89-year-old female presented with worsening lower extremity edema, dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, weight loss, early satiety, and generalized abdominal pain. Initial imaging (CT abdomen/pelvis) revealed a large (15x22x23 cm) solid and cystic intraperitoneal mass with cystic necrosis and mass effect on surrounding organs. Biopsy of tissue samples characterized a spindle cell tumor, suggestive of a GIST, and molecular testing showed an exon 11 mutation (PDGFRA-mutant negative), with radiological staging of III T4N0M0. The patient deferred surgical resection but started targeted molecular therapy with imatinib 100 mg twice daily. Initial symptoms of edema, dyspnea, and orthopnea improved with diuretics.
